Order No. 06/Dated: 10 April, 2024
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Apprehending his arrest in connection with Lohsinghna P.S. Case No. 221/2022 registered under
Sections 341, 342, 323, 498A, 504, 506, 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 & 4 of the Dowry
Prohibition Act, petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per the FIR, the allegation against the petitioner is that the informant was married with this petitioner on 13.12.2021 in accordance with Hindu rites and rituals.
There is demand of car, due to which, the informant was tortured and subjected to cruelty and ultimately driven out from her matrimonial house.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather all the allegations are false and fabricated against him.
It is further submitted that due to incompatibility of temperament between the informant and petitioner, this false case has been instituted.
It is further submitted that the mediation was undertaken between the parties before the court below and informant was living with the petitioner.

It is further submitted that petitioner is a student and could not fulfill the illegal demand of the informant, due to which, again she could not adjust in Page 1|2 the family of the petitioner and returned back to her parental home.
Petitioner undertakes to cooperate in investigation and abide with all terms and conditions, as imposed by this Hon'ble Court, in case of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Hence,
petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Learned APP appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 have vehemently opposed the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner and have submitted that inspite of conciliation before the lower court, petitioner had failed to keep his wife / informant with due dignity and honour and she was compelled to reside in her parental home with her widow mother and also there is direct allegation of demand of Car.
Hence, petitioner does not deserve the privilege of anticipatory bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record and also in view of the fact that there is allegation and counter allegation between the parties due to domestic dispute, I am inclined to extend privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Twenty five thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned A.C.J.M., Hazaribag, in connection with Lohsinghna P.S.
Case No. 221/2022 with condition that he will cooperate in investigation and furnish his mobile number and photocopy of the Aadhar Card with an undertaking that he will not change his mobile number during the pendency of the case and subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sunil/ Page 2|2 Shorya Singh @ Sourya Singh vs The State Of Jharkhand on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59864276/
